html:
A religion founded in southern Vietnam in 1926 that draws together Buddhism, Taoism, Confucianism, Christianity and spirit worship under one God, the Cao Đài or "High Tower".

It grew out of séances held by Vietnamese civil servants under French rule, who believed spirits spoke to them. The faith was formally founded in 1926 and built its Holy See at Tây Ninh, near the Cambodian border. Its symbol is the Divine Eye.

Caodaists honour the Buddha, Confucius, Laozi and Jesus as earlier revelations. They also venerate saints from outside Asia, most famously the French writer Victor Hugo, along with Sun Yat-sen. Its church has a pope and a hierarchy modelled on the Catholic one. Believers pray, honour their ancestors and often keep a vegetarian diet.

The religion grew fast among southern peasants and by the 1940s had its own army, which played a part in the wars of the following decades. After 1975 the communist government seized its lands and curbed it. It still has millions of followers, mostly in the south.
sum: A religion founded in southern Vietnam in 1926 that draws together Buddhism, Taoism, Confucianism, Christianity and spirit worship under one God, the Cao Đài or "High Tower".
